_doc: Package C2: one trade, landmark, named NPC and rumour set per settlement (WorldGen NAMES order = settlement id). `alias` = the poster name shown instead (Oakvale = Greenhollow, Ironmarch = Silverford). Landmark parts use the RegionSites part format plus 'free:'/'r1:' keys (see tools/region1/gen_world_data.py). Consumed by scripts/world/region1_world.gd (sites) and scripts/world/region1_identity.gd (rumours).

settlements.name: Ashford
settlements.trade: Milling and the hearth: the stream turns the mill, the ring of stones keeps the dark out.

npcs.name: Maren Coldbrook
npcs.greet: Staff up. Feet apart. No, the other apart.
npcs.trade: Ashford lives by the mill and the ring: every child learns the staff in this yard, and every child learns to touch the stones.
lines: Not bad. Not good. Not bad. Come back when your grip stops trembling.
Forty slept the night I held the stone. Fair trade. Don't tell your mother I said so.
The Miller's Stone sang a little flat last week. Idra says stones get tired. I say so do I.

npc.name: Maren Coldbrook
npc.greet: Staff up. Feet apart. No, the other apart.
npc.trade: Ashford lives by the mill and the ring: every child learns the staff in this yard, and every child learns to touch the stones.
lines: Not bad. Not good. Not bad. Come back when your grip stops trembling.
Forty slept the night I held the stone. Fair trade. Don't tell your mother I said so.
The Miller's Stone sang a little flat last week. Idra says stones get tired. I say so do I.

rumours: The Miller's Stone hums flat some evenings. Idra Vell says it is only tired.
The Guard has nine spears for forty-one stones. Captain Hollis counts them like sheep.
Children who beat Maren Coldbrook at staves get honey cakes. Nobody has yet.
Somebody left a lantern on the Miller's Stone at dusk. Nobody will say who.

settlements.name: Kingsreach
settlements.trade: Crown and court: the Council of Wardens sits here, the tournaments are run here, the great market is here.

npcs.name: Herald Corwin Vale
npcs.greet: Hear ye. Well, hear me, at least.
npcs.trade: Kingsreach is where Valencious decides things: the Council of Wardens, the Royal Ember Academy and the Midsummer tourney all answer to this one hill.
lines: The Crown Princess rode out with four guards and came back with six more. Nobody knows where they came from.
The Wardens vote on the stones each Kindling Night. The vote is always 'more hands'. The hands never come.
The Dawn Throne's envoy has taken the old chapel. The King let him. Make of that what you will.

npc.name: Herald Corwin Vale

The Dawn Throne's envoy has taken the old chapel. The King let him. Make of that what you will.

rumours: The Crown Princess rode out with four guards and came back with six.
The Council voted 'more hands for the stones' again. The hands are still not here.
The Dawn Throne's envoy took the old chapel by the north road. The King allowed it.
The Academy is scouting: a scholar in blue asked after children who can make the stones hum.

settlements.name: Millbrook
settlements.trade: Flour and bread: the great windmill grinds the vale's wheat; the bakehouse feeds three villages.

npcs.name: Hob Millwright
npcs.greet: Mind the sails and mind your hat.
npcs.trade: Millbrook's windmill grinds the flour for the whole vale; the smell of its bakehouse is the first thing travellers mention.
lines: The sails turned backward on their own last Tuesday. Swear to it. Flour everywhere.
Redwater dyers pay in cloth, Thornfield brewers pay in ale. I prefer the ale.
A sack of Millbrook flour is good luck on a road with no stones. Take two.

npc.name: Hob Millwright
npc.greet: Mind the sails and mind your hat.
npc.trade: Millbrook's windmill grinds the flour for the whole vale; the smell of its bakehouse is the first thing travellers mention.

Redwater dyers pay in cloth, Thornfield brewers pay in ale. I prefer the ale.
A sack of Millbrook flour is good luck on a road with no stones. Take two.

rumours: The mill sails turned backward on their own last Tuesday. Flour everywhere.
Thornfield's brewer pays for barley in ale. The miller prefers that.
A sack of Millbrook flour is said to be good luck on a stoneless road.
The east road is quiet. Quieter than it should be, says the baker.

settlements.name: Stonehollow
settlements.trade: Cut stone: its quarry squared the stones of half the vale's waymarks, and its masons carve for the Guild at Silverford.

npcs.name: Brenna Flint
npcs.greet: Stone doesn't care how your morning went.
npcs.trade: Stonehollow cuts the stone: every waymark on the Ember Road came from this quarry, and every Silverford mason starts here.
lines: A good waystone takes three weeks to cut and a day to crack. Cheaper to keep them lit, I say.
We sent forty blocks to Silverford for the Guild. Odrin Thale paid late and apologised well.
The deep face hums at night. Not the stones; the rock. It remembers being mountain.

npc.name: Brenna Flint
npc.greet: Stone doesn't care how your morning went.

rumours: A good waystone takes three weeks to cut and a day to crack, says the quarrymaster.
The deep quarry face hums at night. The masons have stopped working past dusk.
Silverford's Guild ordered forty blocks and paid late, but apologised well.
A cart of green-veined stone went north with a Runeward escort. Nobody says where.

settlements.name: Eastmere
settlements.trade: Milk, butter and cheese: the eastern pastures' herds come home to Eastmere's dairy.

npcs.name: Tilda Marsh
npcs.greet: Mind the pail, it's still warm.
npcs.trade: Eastmere's herds are the vale's largest: cheese wheels from this dairy go west as far as Kingsreach's tables.
lines: The spotted cow prefers the roadside verge. She knows which stones are dark. Clever girl.
We send cheese to Silverford for the Solkar traders. They pay in saffron. I don't know what to do with saffron.
Eastmere's butter keeps three weeks in a cold cellar. Four if the Runeward blesses the cellar.

npc.name: Tilda Marsh
npc.greet: Mind the pail, it's still warm.
npc.trade: Eastmere's herds are the vale's largest: cheese wheels from this dairy go west as far as Kingsreach's tables.

We send cheese to Silverford for the Solkar traders. They pay in saffron. I don't know what to do with saffron.
Eastmere's butter keeps three weeks in a cold cellar. Four if the Runeward blesses the cellar.

rumours: The spotted cow prefers the roadside verge. She seems to know which stones are dark.
Saffron has arrived at the dairy. Nobody ordered saffron.
Eastmere butter keeps three weeks in a cold cellar, four if a warden blesses it.
Wolves took no sheep this year. Wolves took a dairy cart, on the east road, in daylight.

settlements.name: Redwater
settlements.trade: Dyes and cloth: madder red, woad blue and weld gold steep in the vats along the stream.

npcs.name: Mirel Redhand
npcs.greet: Don't shake my hand; you'll be red until Tuesday.
npcs.trade: Redwater's dyers colour half the vale's cloth: their red is the Crown's red, and the Guild's blue comes from their woad vats.
lines: Royal blue is woad and a lot of patience. Silverford pays double for the good batch.
The stream runs red on dye days. Children in the next valley think it is an omen. We let them.
Somebody stole a bolt of Highwatch blue. The thief is easy to spot. He is the man who is not wearing it.

npc.name: Mirel Redhand
npc.greet: Don't shake my hand; you'll be red until Tuesday.
npc.trade: Redwater's dyers colour half the vale's cloth: their red is the Crown's red, and the Guild's blue comes from their woad vats.

rumours: The stream runs red on dye days. Children downstream think it is an omen.
A bolt of Highwatch blue went missing. The thief should be easy to spot.
Silverford pays double for the good woad batch, and complains the price.
The Solkar traders want a yellow we don't know how to make.

settlements.name: Thornfield
settlements.trade: Barley and ale: Thornfield's brewery and tithe barn; its hedgerows of thorn keep the fields safe.

npcs.name: Hesta Thorne
npcs.greet: First pint is free if you can name the hop.
npcs.trade: Thornfield's barley goes into the vale's ale, and its thorn hedges have kept the wolves off the fields for three generations.
lines: Thorn hedges hold better than stones, some years. Wolves hate the scratch; stones hate the wear.
My ale won a Kingsreach prize. The Council gave a scroll. I asked for gold. They sent a second scroll.
The tithe barn is half full. Half. After a good harvest. Somebody is sitting on the rest.

npc.name: Hesta Thorne
npc.greet: First pint is free if you can name the hop.
npc.trade: Thornfield's barley goes into the vale's ale, and its thorn hedges have kept the wolves off the fields for three generations.

The tithe barn is half full. Half. After a good harvest. Somebody is sitting on the rest.

rumours: Thorn hedges hold better than stones some years, says the brewmistress.
The tithe barn stands half empty after a good harvest. Someone has been sitting on the rest.
Thornfield ale won a Kingsreach prize and a scroll. The brewer wanted gold.
A Church envoy's cart passed east and did not stop to buy ale. The brewer took it personally.

settlements.name: Greywatch
settlements.trade: Spears and discipline: the Greywatch Spear Hall drills the militia that marches under the Order of the Highwatch.

npcs.name: Sergeant Ulric Greyspear
npcs.greet: Shoulders back. The spear is not a walking stick.
npcs.trade: Greywatch trains the spear line for the north: the Order's recruits come through this hall before they see Highwatch.
lines: Spears up, feet planted, and do not look at the wolf. Look at the man next to you.
The Order sent us forty recruits. Thirty stayed. Twenty can hold a line. Ten can keep it.
Sir Rowan Ashby says a knight is a spearman who did not quit. Rowan would.

npc.name: Sergeant Ulric Greyspear
npc.greet: Shoulders back. The spear is not a walking stick.
npc.trade: Greywatch trains the spear line for the north: the Order's recruits come through this hall before they see Highwatch.

rumours: The Order sent forty recruits to the Spear Hall. Thirty stayed, ten can hold a line.
Sergeant Greyspear says a knight is just a spearman who did not quit.
The watch-fires at Highwatch burned twice last week. Nobody will say why.
Drums on the north wind after dusk. The sergeant says it is the wind.

settlements.name: Oakvale
settlements.trade: Crops and the great oak: Greenhollow's south meadows feed the vale; the Pennick farm is the largest.

npcs.name: Gilda Pennick
npcs.greet: If you're here for eggs, the hens are sulking.
npcs.trade: Greenhollow's south fields are the vale's bread: the Pennick farm brings in a third of the harvest, and the Great Oak is older than the village.
lines: The south fields have gone strange at the edge. Violet. Only a little. I'm told it's the light.
We tithe to the Crown in wheat and to the Runeward in bread. The Runeward eat better.
My barn burned once. Only the once. I keep the old scorch on the beam so the new barn remembers.

npc.name: Gilda Pennick
npc.greet: If you're here for eggs, the hens are sulking.
npc.trade: Greenhollow's south fields are the vale's bread: the Pennick farm brings in a third of the harvest, and the Great Oak is older than the village.

rumours: The south fields have gone violet at the edge. Only a little. Somebody says it's the light.
The Great Oak hums in a storm. Gilda Pennick insists it always has.
The Runeward eat better than the Crown's tax men; Greenhollow bread has a lot to do with it.
Wolves came to the hedge at noon. Not at night. At noon.

settlements.name: Highcliff
settlements.trade: Steel and horses: the armourers and stablers who outfit the knights of Highwatch Keep on the ridge above.

npcs.name: Dagna Holt
npcs.greet: Steel's honest. People aren't. Show me your blade.
npcs.trade: Highcliff outfits the Order of the Highwatch: the lancers' mail is hammered here, and the ridge stable breeds the knights' chargers.
lines: Sir Rowan's armour has been mended eleven times. He refuses to buy new. Says it remembers his knees.
Steel from Hollowdeep comes south through Kingsreach. The price of it is a crime.
The chargers know the road to the pass. They won't go past the last banner. Smart animals.

rumours: Sir Rowan Ashby's armour has been mended eleven times. He refuses new.
The chargers will not go past the last banner on the north road. Smart animals.
A knight rode down from Highwatch with frost on his cloak in midsummer.
Hollowdeep steel is three times the price this season.

settlements.name: Brackenmoor
settlements.trade: Pelts and venison: a hunters' hold on the edge of the wild, where every hunter carries a wolf-tooth token.

npcs.name: Garrick Bracken
npcs.greet: Keep your voice down. The bracken listens.
npcs.trade: Brackenmoor hunts what the stones do not reach: its pelts and venison feed the frontier, and its hunters know every den by smell.
lines: Wolves came in from the east ridge at noon last week. Noon. They have learned the stones are tired.
A white hart was seen in the north wood, antlers like a cathedral. We do not shoot the white hart.
If you see a den, tell me before you tell the Guard. The Guard counts. I hunt.

npc.name: Garrick Bracken
npc.greet: Keep your voice down. The bracken listens.

rumours: Wolves came down from the east ridge at noon last week. They have learned the stones are tired.
A white hart was seen in the north wood, antlers like a cathedral. Nobody shoots the white hart.
The huntmaster pays for news of dens, and double for news of wasps.
Hunters say the bog to the west has started singing at night.

settlements.name: Westfen
settlements.trade: Herbs and peat: the marsh's boardwalks, reed huts and herb racks; the only healers who will walk into the fen.

npcs.name: Nessa Fenn
npcs.greet: Wipe your boots. The moss minds.
npcs.trade: Westfen's herbwives are the only healers who will walk the fen at night, and the boardwalk keeps the marsh from swallowing the road.
lines: The toads are bigger this year. Bog toads. Long tongue, short temper. Don't step on the pretty ones.
Westfen tea cures fever. It also cures company. People don't stay to ask for a second cup.
Something sings under the boards when the wind is west. The Veyl rangers say it is only the marsh.

npc.name: Nessa Fenn
npc.greet: Wipe your boots. The moss minds.

rumours: The bog toads are bigger this year. Long tongue, short temper.
Westfen tea cures fever. It also cures company.
Something sings under the boards when the wind is from the west.
Veyl rangers passed through, speaking of a black fen further south-west.

settlements.name: Ironmarch
settlements.trade: Crafts and contracts: the Masons' and Runecarvers' Guild, the Merchants' Hall and the Adventurers' branch all keep hall here by the ford.

npcs.name: Odrin Thale
npcs.greet: Irritatingly clean, my ledgers. You may look.
npcs.trade: Silverford is where the vale's crafts are licensed: no stone is carved, no contract sealed and no caravan weighed without the Guild's mark.
lines: The Guild holds the only licence to cut a waystone. The Crown holds the only licence to be angry about it.
A Solkar mistress has paid the Hall in sunstone oil. It burns silver. Nobody asks how.
We count stones for the Runeward. The count, I confess, has been... generous.

npc.name: Odrin Thale
npc.greet: Irritatingly clean, my ledgers. You may look.
npc.trade: Silverford is where the vale's crafts are licensed: no stone is carved, no contract sealed and no caravan weighed without the Guild's mark.

We count stones for the Runeward. The count, I confess, has been... generous.

rumours: The Guild alone may cut a waystone; the Crown alone may be angry about it.
A Solkar caravan mistress paid the Hall in sunstone oil. It burns silver.
The Merchants' Hall is buying iron at any price. Somebody is arming somebody.
Guild ledgers say forty stones are lit. Wardens say twenty-six. One of them is counting wrong.

settlements.name: Saltwick
settlements.trade: Salt and dried fish: the far south-west's salt pans and fish-racks, every wagon south of the stones smells of Saltwick.

npcs.name: Orla Saltmaster
npcs.greet: Lick the wall if you don't believe me.
npcs.trade: Saltwick's pans are the vale's pantry: salted fish and sea-salt go north along the frontier road, and nothing keeps a winter like Saltwick salt.
lines: A pinch of Saltwick salt on the doorstep keeps the small dark things out. Also the neighbours.
The last caravan never made it past the Emberfall Roadhouse. Bandits, or worse: bad weather.
Frontier roads have few stones. We salt the verge. Wolves hate a salted track.

npc.name: Orla Saltmaster
npc.greet: Lick the wall if you don't believe me.

rumours: A pinch of salt on the doorstep keeps small dark things out, say Saltwick folk.
The last salt caravan never made it past the Emberfall Roadhouse.
Wolves hate a salted track; Saltwick salts its verges where the stones are few.
The far pans have a sheen no salt should have.

settlements.name: Cindermoor
settlements.trade: Charcoal and smelting: Cindermoor's kilns burn the moorland oak that feeds the vale's forges.

npcs.name: Dov Sutt
npcs.greet: Don't breathe near the kiln. Or do. I'm not your mother.
npcs.trade: Cindermoor burns the moorland oak to charcoal; every forge from Stonehollow to Highcliff cooks on Cindermoor black.
lines: Smoke on the moor after dusk is ours. If it's smoke you can't smell, it isn't.
Charcoal costs more this year. The forests are thinner. Somebody is cutting beyond the ward.
The far kiln was cold when I woke. No fire, no ash, not even the scorch on the ground. Odd.

rumours: Smoke on the moor after dusk is ours. If you can't smell it, it is not.
Charcoal costs more this year: someone is cutting trees beyond the ward.
A kiln went cold overnight with no ash and no scorch left.
Dov Sutt swears the old moor road has a stone nobody carved.

settlements.name: Dunhallow
settlements.trade: Carts and wheels: the wheelwrights and carters of the north-west, where every wagon on the vale's roads was mended at least once.

npcs.name: Wynn Cartwright
npcs.greet: Never trust a wheel that squeaks. It's telling you something.
npcs.trade: Dunhallow mends the wheels of the world: every caravan that crosses the vale's far roads stops here for an axle and a bowl of soup.
lines: A wheel lasts four hundred miles on stone road and forty on none. Do the maths on the frontier.
I fixed a Solkar wagon. Wheels were different. Wider. They roll in sand, so, fewer stones.
The Dunhallow road to Ashford is the longest ungarrisoned track in the vale. Take a spare axle.

npc.name: Wynn Cartwright
npc.greet: Never trust a wheel that squeaks. It's telling you something.

rumours: A wheel lasts four hundred miles on stone road and forty on none.
Dunhallow fixed a Solkar wagon with wide desert wheels. Carters are still arguing.
The Dunhallow road to Ashford is the longest ungarrisoned track in the vale.
A wagon-train lost a wheel near the old beacon and the carters came home without a driver.

settlements.name: Wolfsend
settlements.trade: Watch and wolf-hunting: the easternmost village, where the ditch-and-stake watch keeps an eye on the Eastern Gate road.

npcs.name: Carrow Dunmere
npcs.greet: Eastward is the Gate. Westward is home. Wolves are everywhere.
npcs.trade: Wolfsend is the vale's last village before the Eastern Gate: its watchmen turn back pilgrims, hunt wolves and sell wolf-tooth luck.
lines: The Gate's shut. Church's order. Pilgrims queue at the ditch and wait. We feed them, nobody asked.
Wolves come at dawn this month, not dusk. Hunters say it's the moon. The hunters are wrong.
A rider came through at night, sunlit banner under his cloak. He did not stop. Horse was lathered.

rumours: The Eastern Gate is shut by the Patriarch's order. Pilgrims queue at the ditch.
Wolves come at dawn this month, not at dusk.
A rider with a sun-banner under his cloak crossed at night and did not stop.
Wolf-tooth luck sells well in Wolfsend. Hunters wear it; the pilgrims buy it.

settlements.name: Harrowgate
settlements.trade: The south gate of the vale: every caravan from the Solkar road stages here, and the harrow arch marks the last stones before the desert track.

npcs.name: Kavi ar-Sunhaven
npcs.greet: Saffron, cardamom, sunstone salt. Smell first, argue after.
npcs.trade: Harrowgate is the vale's southern door: the Solkar caravans from the desert come up this road, and the spice smell reaches Emberfall on a south wind.
lines: Midsummer we go north to the Fair at Silverford. The spice price doubles by the Guild's hall. It's fair, it's only mathematics.
Our wagons have wide wheels for sand. Your stone roads are too narrow. We drive on the verge. The verge is quite full.
Sunstone oil burns silver. A drop on a dark stone makes it glow for an hour. Don't tell the Runeward; they'd buy all of it.

rumours: Solkar caravans are due at the Midsummer Fair. The spice price doubles by Silverford.
Sunstone oil, a drop on a dark stone, makes it glow for an hour. The Runeward would buy all of it.
The south road is quiet but for Solkar wagons, and the wagons say it is very busy in the desert.
An old arch on the south road: the Harrow. Nobody knows who built it. The spice-merchants bow.

settlements.name: Emberfall
settlements.trade: Glass and ember-crystal: a star fell here in the old days, and Emberfall's glassblowers have worked its red glass since.
settlements.tagline: Glass Kilns and the Fallen Star

label.sub: Glass Kilns and the Fallen Star

npcs.name: Teyo Emberglass
npcs.greet: Red glass, hot and honest. Mind the heat.
npcs.trade: Emberfall's red glass is the vale's rarest craft: the fallen star's crystal gives it its glow, and the lantern-makers of Silverford pay in silver.
lines: The crystal hums when the stones dim. I'm not saying it means anything. I'm saying it hums.
Wind from the south brings spice. Wind from the west brings cold. Wind from the Scar brings nothing. That's worse.
A Solkar trader wanted a window for a desert temple. I made it. It was the reddest thing I have ever seen.

npc.name: Teyo Emberglass
npc.greet: Red glass, hot and honest. Mind the heat.
npc.trade: Emberfall's red glass is the vale's rarest craft: the fallen star's crystal gives it its glow, and the lantern-makers of Silverford pay in silver.
lines: The crystal hums when the stones dim. I'm not saying it means anything. I'm saying it hums.
Wind from the south brings spice. Wind from the west brings cold. Wind from the Scar brings nothing. That's worse.
A Solkar trader wanted a window for a desert temple. I made it. It was the reddest thing I have ever seen.

rumours: Emberfall's crystal hums whenever a stone goes dim.
Wind from the south brings spice, the west brings cold. Wind from the Scar brings nothing, and that is worse.
The lantern makers of Silverford pay in silver for Emberfall red glass.
A fallen-star fragment went missing from the kiln. The glass was bluer the next day.

settlements.name: Ravenscar
settlements.trade: Furs and ravens: the last village before Grimfen Pass, where trappers watch the snowline and ravens watch the trappers.

npcs.name: Ulla Crowe
npcs.greet: Ravens are listening. Don't say anything you'd regret.
npcs.trade: Ravenscar trades furs for grain: the trappers know the snowline, and they are the only ones who have seen Grimfen Pass this century.
lines: The Pass has been shut since the Long Dark. Snow is the lock. The key is spring, if spring ever comes up there.
We've found bones bigger than a cart below the ridge. Horned. Frosted. Nothing alive has horns that long.
On clear winter nights the north sky goes green. The ravens go quiet. So do we.

npc.name: Ulla Crowe
npc.greet: Ravens are listening. Don't say anything you'd regret.
npc.trade: Ravenscar trades furs for grain: the trappers know the snowline, and they are the only ones who have seen Grimfen Pass this century.

rumours: The Pass has been shut since the Long Dark. Snow is the lock, and spring is the key.
Trappers found bones bigger than a cart below the ridge. Horned, and frosted.
On clear winter nights the north sky goes green and the ravens go quiet.
A Highwatch knight came up to watch the snowline. He stayed three days and left his tent.

settlements.name: Longmeadow
settlements.trade: Wool and fairs: the long meadows north of the Silverrun feed the vale's flocks, and the autumn fair on the green is the biggest market between the stones and the sea.

npcs.name: Marta Fairwood
npcs.greet: Wool by the stone, fleece by the cart, gossip free.
npcs.trade: Longmeadow's autumn fair sets the price of wool for the whole vale, and nobody sells a fleece before the reeve rings the bell.
lines: The fair-reeve rings the bell at dawn. Sell a fleece before it and the whole green hears about it.
Flocks are down this year. The wolves are bolder past the Silverrun.
Caravans bring spice from the south and leave with wool. Mostly. Sometimes they leave with less.

npc.name: Marta Fairwood
npc.greet: Wool by the stone, fleece by the cart, gossip free.
npc.trade: Longmeadow's autumn fair sets the price of wool for the whole vale, and nobody sells a fleece before the reeve rings the bell.
lines: The fair-reeve rings the bell at dawn. Sell a fleece before it and the whole green hears about it.
Flocks are down this year. The wolves are bolder past the Silverrun.
Caravans bring spice from the south and leave with wool. Mostly. Sometimes they leave with less.

rumours: The autumn fair is the richest day of the year. Thieves know it too.
Wool prices climb every time the eastern road closes.
A shepherd swears a white ram leads the flock home in the fog.
Fair-reeve Marta keeps a ledger of every fleece sold since the Long Dark.

settlements.name: Blackwater
settlements.trade: The ferry and the garrison: Blackwater holds the crossing on the outer road, and every cart pays the toll to the watch.

npcs.name: Sergeant Holt
npcs.greet: Toll is a copper a cart. Walkers are free. Fighters are welcome.
npcs.trade: Blackwater's watch keeps the ford open and the road toll honest, and rides out when the outer road goes quiet.
lines: Coin first, questions after. That is the order at Blackwater.
If the road goes silent for a day, we ride. Last time we found the cart and nobody else.
The garrison needs hands. Pay is poor, the stories are good.

npc.name: Sergeant Holt
npc.greet: Toll is a copper a cart. Walkers are free. Fighters are welcome.
npc.trade: Blackwater's watch keeps the ford open and the road toll honest, and rides out when the outer road goes quiet.
lines: Coin first, questions after. That is the order at Blackwater.
If the road goes silent for a day, we ride. Last time we found the cart and nobody else.
The garrison needs hands. Pay is poor, the stories are good.

rumours: The watch rode out three nights ago and came back with fewer men.
The ford floods with the first thaw. Carts wait a week.
A toll-keeper swears the black water takes a coin every spring.
Bandits ask the watch the toll before they hit the road. A joke, sort of.

settlements.name: Frostmere
settlements.trade: Smoked fish and furs: Frostmere's racks stay cold from autumn to spring, and its trappers know every track north of the mere.

npcs.name: Ulf Greybeard
npcs.greet: If the smoke is thin, the fish is good.
npcs.trade: Frostmere's smokehouses cure the mere's whitefish for the whole north, and its trappers sell pelts to every caravan that braves the road.
lines: Thin smoke, good fish. Thick smoke, the neighbours are burning something they shouldn't.
The mere froze early. The ice sings at night.
A trapper went north in autumn and came back without his dogs.

npc.name: Ulf Greybeard
npc.greet: If the smoke is thin, the fish is good.
npc.trade: Frostmere's smokehouses cure the mere's whitefish for the whole north, and its trappers sell pelts to every caravan that braves the road.
lines: Thin smoke, good fish. Thick smoke, the neighbours are burning something they shouldn't.
The mere froze early. The ice sings at night.
A trapper went north in autumn and came back without his dogs.

rumours: The ice on Frostmere sings at night. Fishers stay ashore.
Trappers found a wolf track the size of a plate.
Smoked whitefish keeps a winter. Smoked wolf, nobody has tried.
A hermit lives past the north shore and trades only in silence.

settlements.name: Amberley
settlements.trade: Honey and beeswax: Amberley's hives line every hedge, and its candles light the shrines of the whole outer road.

npcs.name: Edda Hivewarden
npcs.greet: Hold still. If one lands, it is deciding about you.
npcs.trade: Amberley's hives give honey for mead and wax for candles; every wayshrine on the outer road burns Amberley wax.
lines: Never swat. Bow. They notice manners.
Candles burn longer if you hum while you pour. Nobody knows why.
The wild bees nest in the old tower. Nobody wants that honey.

npc.name: Edda Hivewarden
npc.greet: Hold still. If one lands, it is deciding about you.
npc.trade: Amberley's hives give honey for mead and wax for candles; every wayshrine on the outer road burns Amberley wax.
lines: Never swat. Bow. They notice manners.
Candles burn longer if you hum while you pour. Nobody knows why.
The wild bees nest in the old tower. Nobody wants that honey.

rumours: A swarm settled on the shrine road and will not leave.
Amberley mead is stronger than it tastes. Travellers learn once.
Wax candles from Amberley are said to keep the dark out for an hour more.
The hive in the old tower hums in a key nobody can name.

settlements.name: Skarholm
settlements.trade: Ore and coal: Skarholm's shafts feed the vale's forges, and the carters leave heavy and come back light.

npcs.name: Brann Coalhand
npcs.greet: Mind the cart. It does not mind you.
npcs.trade: Skarholm's yard sorts ore from the north shafts and ships it to every forge on the outer road; coal black is the town's colour.
lines: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the soul, not the stew.
The north shaft is closed again. The foreman says it is the roof. The miners say it is not.
We pay well. We pay in coal when the coin runs short.

npc.name: Brann Coalhand
npc.greet: Mind the cart. It does not mind you.
npc.trade: Skarholm's yard sorts ore from the north shafts and ships it to every forge on the outer road; coal black is the town's colour.
lines: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the soul, not the stew.
The north shaft is closed again. The foreman says it is the roof. The miners say it is not.
We pay well. We pay in coal when the coin runs short.

rumours: The north shaft was sealed after a night of knocking from below.
Skarholm iron rings a different note. Smiths can tell.
A carter says the ore wagons weigh more going out than they did coming in.
The yard boss keeps a lantern burning for the miners who did not come up.

settlements.name: Thistledown
settlements.trade: Sheep and spinning: Thistledown's wethers graze the downs, and its spinners sell the finest thread on the outer road.

npcs.name: Wenna Spindle
npcs.greet: Mind the wool. It sticks to everything, especially opinions.
npcs.trade: Thistledown spins the downs' wool into thread; its spinners' guild sets the thread price from here to the stones.
lines: Spin clockwise on a good day and anticlockwise on a bad one. The wool knows.
Sheep go missing near the old barrow. The shepherds do not look for them.
A good thread is worth more than a good sword in winter.

npc.name: Wenna Spindle
npc.greet: Mind the wool. It sticks to everything, especially opinions.
npc.trade: Thistledown spins the downs' wool into thread; its spinners' guild sets the thread price from here to the stones.
lines: Spin clockwise on a good day and anticlockwise on a bad one. The wool knows.
Sheep go missing near the old barrow. The shepherds do not look for them.
A good thread is worth more than a good sword in winter.

rumours: Sheep vanish near the downs' old barrow and nobody goes looking.
Thistledown thread is stronger than rope and half the price.
The spinners sing while they work. The songs are older than the village.
A lamb was born with silver wool. It lasted a day.

settlements.name: Marrowick
settlements.trade: Hides and leather: Marrowick's tanneries stink for a mile, and every saddle on the outer road was cut here.

npcs.name: Garrick Tanner
npcs.greet: You will smell it before you see it. That is the business.
npcs.trade: Marrowick's tanneries cure hide for saddles, boots and harness; the smell is the price of the finest leather in the outer ring.
lines: Wind from the west and the whole town can breathe. Wind from the east and we hold our noses together.
Good leather needs time, oak bark and a strong stomach.
Wolf pelts sell high this season. So do the ones who bring them.

npc.name: Garrick Tanner
npc.greet: You will smell it before you see it. That is the business.
npc.trade: Marrowick's tanneries cure hide for saddles, boots and harness; the smell is the price of the finest leather in the outer ring.
lines: Wind from the west and the whole town can breathe. Wind from the east and we hold our noses together.
Good leather needs time, oak bark and a strong stomach.
Wolf pelts sell high this season. So do the ones who bring them.

rumours: The river runs brown below Marrowick. Fishermen go upstream.
A rider's saddle from Marrowick is said to hold a seat through a gallop and a storm.
The tannery cat has been there longer than the tannery.
Hunters bring pelts at dusk and do not stay for supper.

settlements.name: Coldharbor
settlements.trade: Boats and rope: Coldharbor's slip builds the ferries and flat boats that cross the Silverrun, and its ropewalk is a quarter mile long.

npcs.name: Ysolde Rope
npcs.greet: If it floats, we built it. If it sank, somebody else did.
npcs.trade: Coldharbor builds the river's boats and twists its rope; every ferry on the Silverrun was laid down on this slip.
lines: A boat is promises held together with pitch. Break one, break the other.
The river freezes late. Ferries run until the first snow, and sometimes after.
We built one boat with a keel of black oak. It never leaked and never came back.

npc.name: Ysolde Rope
npc.greet: If it floats, we built it. If it sank, somebody else did.
npc.trade: Coldharbor builds the river's boats and twists its rope; every ferry on the Silverrun was laid down on this slip.
lines: A boat is promises held together with pitch. Break one, break the other.
The river freezes late. Ferries run until the first snow, and sometimes after.
We built one boat with a keel of black oak. It never leaked and never came back.

rumours: The ropewalk is a quarter mile long and still too short for the new ferry.
A boatwright swears the river speaks in the spring melt.
One ferry crosses at night. Nobody has seen its pilot.
Coldharbor pitch burns blue. Do not ask why.

settlements.name: Hollowmere
settlements.trade: Reeds and baskets: Hollowmere cuts the mere's reeds for thatch and weaves baskets for every market from here to the capital.

npcs.name: Nell Reedwife
npcs.greet: Tread soft. The mere remembers footsteps.
npcs.trade: Hollowmere cuts the mere's reeds for thatch and weaves baskets by the thousand; a good roof in the outer ring is a Hollowmere roof.
lines: Cut reeds at the low tide of the moon, never the high. The mere does not like greed.
A basket carries more than you think and less than you hope.
Lights on the mere after dark are not ours. We do not follow them.

npc.name: Nell Reedwife
npc.greet: Tread soft. The mere remembers footsteps.
npc.trade: Hollowmere cuts the mere's reeds for thatch and weaves baskets by the thousand; a good roof in the outer ring is a Hollowmere roof.
lines: Cut reeds at the low tide of the moon, never the high. The mere does not like greed.
A basket carries more than you think and less than you hope.
Lights on the mere after dark are not ours. We do not follow them.

rumours: Lights drift over the mere after midnight. The reed-cutters do not follow them.
A Hollowmere roof outlasts three storms and one landlord.
Baskets from here are said to keep bread fresh a week.
An old woman talks to the mere and says it answers.

settlements.name: Duskwater
settlements.trade: Lanterns and night fishing: Duskwater's fishers work by lamplight, and its glassworkers sell lanterns to every road inn.

npcs.name: Orsen Wick
npcs.greet: A lamp is only a promise to come home. Buy two.
npcs.trade: Duskwater's night fishers hang lanterns over the water to draw the shoals, and its lantern-makers keep every road inn lit.
lines: Night fishing needs light and silence. Most of us can only manage the first.
A lantern left burning on the pier brings the boats home. Mostly.
The old fishers say the dark water has a second bottom.

npc.name: Orsen Wick
npc.greet: A lamp is only a promise to come home. Buy two.
npc.trade: Duskwater's night fishers hang lanterns over the water to draw the shoals, and its lantern-makers keep every road inn lit.
lines: Night fishing needs light and silence. Most of us can only manage the first.
A lantern left burning on the pier brings the boats home. Mostly.
The old fishers say the dark water has a second bottom.

rumours: Lanterns on the pier burn all night and the boats still lose their way.
Duskwater lanterns are said to burn through a gale.
A fisher pulled up a glass float with a candle still alight inside.
On still nights you can hear a bell under the water.
